spectral.true_color: Fields range from deep green through muted green to pale tan. Woodland is generally dark green with coarse brightness variations. The central curved strip is unusually bright green, while narrow corridors and some small openings are pale gray or beige. These visible contrasts have high confidence.
spectral.false_color: Many agricultural parcels are vivid red, while pale true-color fields become cyan, gray-green, or muted gray. Woodland ranges from dark burgundy to brighter mottled red. The central curved strip is pink-red, supporting vegetation cover. These observed patterns have high confidence.

implications.claim: Vivid red fields contain substantial photosynthetically active vegetation, although display intensity alone does not measure physiological health.
Cyan and muted agricultural parcels likely have less green vegetation, with exposed soil, dry residue, or recently worked surfaces contributing to their appearance.
The bright green curved strip is vegetated rather than an obvious open-water surface, because it also appears pink-red in false color.
Darker woodland red can result from canopy structure, shadow, or vegetation differences; it does not establish poorer vegetation condition than adjacent fields.
Moisture differences may contribute to tonal variation, but wet and dry surfaces cannot be separated reliably from these displays alone.
No clearly identifiable open-water body is visible, so water turbidity cannot be assessed.
Pale narrow surfaces may include roads or tracks, but their colors do not reliably distinguish pavement, gravel, bare soil, or small roofs.

spectral.not_revealed: These rendered composites do not provide calibrated reflectance, quantitative vegetation indices, soil or canopy moisture, water turbidity, crop identity, canopy height, tree species, surface material, or change through time; high confidence. Display stretching and mixed pixels limit direct radiometric comparisons; high confidence.

uncertainties: Cover percentages are visual estimates, not a classified pixel inventory; several percentage points of uncertainty per major class are plausible, with medium confidence.
The agricultural parcel count is approximate because some boundaries are faint or clipped; medium confidence. Separately listed field features are subsets of the parcel mosaic.
Feature dimensions are estimated from the 1,200 m patch width; medium confidence. Apparent widths near 10 m are especially unreliable.
Grassland, forage crops, other green crops, and low woody vegetation can overlap spectrally and spatially at this resolution; high confidence.
Bare soil, dry residue, senescent crops, and lightly vegetated surfaces are ambiguous within pale fields; high confidence.
Roads, drainage lines, and narrow clearings may resemble one another where they cross dark vegetation; medium confidence.
Small buildings, vehicles, individual trees, ditches, fences, and narrow hedgerows cannot be resolved reliably; high confidence.
Dark patches may combine canopy shading, illumination effects, and vegetation differences; medium confidence. Terrain relief cannot be determined securely.
Upsampling, interpolation, image stretching, and mixed pixels may exaggerate smoothness, width, or color at boundaries; high confidence.
No obvious cloud cover is visible, with high confidence; individual dark areas cannot confidently be labeled cloud shadows.
Season, species, management history, and active change remain uncertain without temporal observations or additional measurements; high confidence.

summaries.w25: An agricultural–woodland mosaic dominates (high confidence), with contrasting field vegetation and a winding access corridor (medium confidence). Season and crop identities remain unresolved.
summaries.w50: Fields dominate the upper and left portions, while woodland occupies much of the east and south (high confidence). Bright-red vegetation contrasts with pale, weakly vegetated parcels (high confidence). A sinuous corridor likely provides access (medium confidence). Crop identities, season, moisture status, and recent management remain unresolved.
summaries.w100: This 1.2 km patch contains an agricultural–woodland mosaic (high confidence), estimated as 48% woody cover, 34% green managed vegetation, 14% pale agricultural surfaces, and 4% corridors or other openings (medium confidence). Angular fields dominate the upper and left portions; woodland is concentrated eastward and southward. Strong red responses indicate abundant active vegetation, while cyan parcels suggest lower green cover (medium confidence). A winding pale corridor likely represents rural access, beside a curved vegetated strip (medium confidence). No clear open-water body or substantial settlement is apparent (medium confidence). Crop types, season, moisture, and management history remain unresolved.
summaries.w200:
The patch is a heterogeneous agricultural–woodland mosaic (high confidence). Visually estimated cover comprises 48% woodland, 34% green managed vegetation, 14% bare or weakly vegetated agricultural parcels, and 4% corridors and other openings (medium confidence). Smooth angular fields occupy much of the upper and left portions, while coarse woody vegetation dominates the east and south. Irregular woodland margins create extensive field edges (high confidence).

A narrow pale corridor crosses the upper fields and becomes sinuous through the center and lower-left portion; interpretation as a road or track has medium confidence. A conspicuous curved green strip beside its central bend also appears pink-red in false color, supporting vegetation cover (high confidence). An isolated pale field lies beside a lower bend.

Vivid-red fields indicate substantial active vegetation, while pale cyan or muted parcels likely contain less green cover (medium confidence). Harvest, fallow, cultivation, and senescence are possible explanations, but none is uniquely established. Woodland darkness may reflect canopy structure and shadow rather than reduced vigor (high confidence).

No clear water body or substantial settlement is apparent (medium confidence). Crop identity, rotation, moisture, forestry activity, climate, and recent change cannot be established from these renderings.
summaries.w400:
This 1.2 × 1.2 km Sentinel-2 patch shows a heterogeneous agricultural–woodland mosaic (high confidence). Approximate visual cover estimates are 48% woodland or dense woody vegetation, 34% green agricultural or managed herbaceous vegetation, 14% pale agricultural surfaces, 3% access corridors and margins, and 1% other openings (medium confidence). These estimates describe apparent cover rather than a measured classification.

The upper-left and upper-center cells contain smooth, angular parcels with contrasting vegetation responses. Several elongated fields run north–south to northwest–southeast. Small agricultural openings also indent the upper-right woodland edge. Across the middle-left and middle-center cells, broad fields transition into irregular woody cover. Woodland dominates the middle-right and much of the bottom row, forming an apparently connected eastern and southern complex (medium confidence).

A narrow pale corridor runs diagonally through the upper fields, curves southward near the center, and continues through pronounced lower bends. A road or track interpretation has medium confidence; continuity and individual segments remain uncertain. Beside the central bend, a curved bright-green strip becomes pink-red in false color, indicating vegetation (high confidence). Pale agricultural bands lie immediately east. A smaller angular pale field borders a lower bend, and an irregular opening occurs farther southwest. Tiny light patches cannot reliably be identified as buildings.

True color separates dark-green woody cover, green fields, and pale tan parcels. False color emphasizes vivid-red vegetation in many fields and darker, mottled red in woodland. This supports abundant active vegetation, but red brightness alone cannot quantify vigor or health (high confidence). Cyan or muted fields probably have reduced green cover, potentially representing exposed soil, residue, senescence, or recent cultivation (medium confidence). Differences in woodland brightness may reflect canopy structure, species, or illumination.

No clearly identifiable open-water body or substantial settlement is apparent (medium confidence). Water turbidity and moisture status cannot be assessed reliably. The images do not establish active irrigation, flooding, erosion, logging, or recent clearing. Agriculture is clear, but crop species, rotation, and forestry management remain unresolved. A temperate growing-season setting is plausible only with low confidence; biome and climate are not diagnostic. Native 10 m resolution, mixed pixels, display stretching, and upsampling limit narrow-feature dimensions and small-object identification (high confidence).
